identity.name: Chronomètre Souverain
identity.one_liner: F.P. Journe's core time-only chronometer, built around a hand-wound movement with an independent seconds deadbeat function and a dial guilloched in the clou de Paris pattern.

narrative.story: Introduced in 2005, the Chronomètre Souverain is F.P. Journe's plainest statement of intent: hours, minutes, small seconds, and a power-reserve indicator, finished to chronometer standard with nothing added to justify the price. It won the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève's Best Men's Watch prize that year, and has stayed in the catalog largely unchanged since, making it the reference against which collectors measure every other Journe complication.
narrative.collector_notes: Dial variants (silver, and later a 'Havana' brown-toned version) and case metal define pricing spread within this reference; the movement architecture and finishing are consistent across variants, so collector premium tracks dial and metal rarity rather than mechanical difference.
